Based on the chest X-ray findings from the follow-up period, what is the most likely radiological outcome observed in the patient's condition at six weeks? Consider changes in the cavities, air-fluid levels, and other relevant findings. 

A) New cavities have formed with increased air-fluid levels, suggesting progression to lung abscess.
B) The largest cavity has resolved completely with no remaining air-fluid level.
C) There is a reduction in the size of the cavities with the absence of air-fluid levels, consistent with resolving pneumatoceles.
D) The cavities have increased in size, and new atelectatic scarring is observed, indicating worsening of the condition.
E) There is an increase in pleural effusion, suggesting a complication of the underlying condition.
F) The air-fluid level remains unchanged, but the cavities have reduced in size, indicating partial resolution.
